_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Built-In-Test (BIT) Anomaly Reporting
summary: Describes the format and content for a Built-In-Test (BIT) Anomaly Report used to assess system health, diagnostic performance, and configuration-specific reliability during production, induction, and recertification testing.
use_relationship:
The BIT Anomaly Report is used to assess system health, diagnostic performance, and configuration-specific reliability during production acceptance testing, post-fielding induction, and recertification testing. The reported data supports failure reporting, analysis, and corrective action processes (e.g., FRACAS); verification of system readiness for fielding or return to service; and identification of trends related to manufacturing defects, maintenance-induced faults, and recurring failure modes. The data is also used to evaluate BIT effectiveness, including fault detection and isolation capability, and to inform safety, airworthiness, and sustainment decisions. BIT anomaly data shall be traceable to specific hardware and software configurations to enable correlation with test results, maintenance actions, and corrective actions.

This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data product resulting from the work task described in the contract SOW.
